key_insight: GA-AMNO separates adaptive mesh learning into two readable parts: physics-guided placement of computation and geometry-aware transport of features before they are aggregated.
engineering_relevance: This matters for PDE neural operators because it improves accuracy and interpretability when the mesh changes, making cross-discretization inference more robust in scientific simulations.
method: Physics-informed adaptive allocation decides where to compute on the mesh.
Gauge-aware low-rank transport maps source features into the target node context before aggregation.
The framework includes conditions for representation-consistent aggregation and analyzes transport error under topology-preserving mesh deformation.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on five PDE benchmarks, where it improves predictive accuracy and the abstract reports controlled intervention and geometric-mismatch analyses supporting the roles of allocation and interaction.
watch_item: Gauge transport adds modeling and implementation complexity, and its benefits may depend on topology-preserving mesh deformations and accurate geometry conditioning.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
